haiku-low.q1: Held for 10 minutes (expires_at = now + 10 min). If not claimed in time, the minute sweep releases it and returns the stock to sale.
haiku-low.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge. If one line is short, Inventory writes nothing, Cart shows the short items, and no charge is requested.
haiku-low.q3: Payment's one-charge-per-order-id row returns the existing charge on repeat, and the provider call uses Idempotency-Key = order id, so no double charge.
haiku-low.q4: The claim fails, so the order is Cancelled as out of stock, the full amount is refunded automatically, and the customer is emailed. Refund status is recorded separately.
haiku-low.q5: Only after OrderConfirmed, when Cart consumes the event and empties itself. On every failure the cart is left unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: Order moves the checkout between steps. Its order record, including status, shows how far each checkout has got.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which stores the event and writes ChargeSucceeded or ChargeDeclined to its outbox. A relay publishes it to the broker, and Order consumes it.
haiku-low.q8: A unique key on the provider event id makes repeats return 200 with no change. Order acts only while Awaiting payment, and a repeated claim does not decrement stock again.
haiku-low.q9: Order sets the status to Payment failed or declined and asks Inventory to release the hold at once. Inventory sets the reservation Released and lowers the reserved count. The trigger is a ChargeDeclined event or a refused charge call.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory's conditional claim decides it: if the hold is still Held and expires_at is in the future, the order is fulfilled; otherwise it is cancelled and refunded.
haiku-low.q11: The refund is marked Failed with a reason and retried with the same refund key. After the retry limit it stays Open in a needs-attention queue with an alert. The document does not set the limit or who is alerted.
haiku-low.q12: Cart empties itself when it consumes the OrderConfirmed event that Order publishes after a successful claim. Open question 4 asks whether it should clear only the ordered lines.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes (expires_at = now + 10 min). If not claimed, the Inventory sweep (every minute) turns Held rows past expires_at into Released and lowers the reserved count, putting stock back on sale.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before charging (reserve, then Awaiting payment and charge). If any line is short, nothing is written: Inventory is all-or-nothing, replies with the short items, order is Rejected (short stock), nothing reserved or charged, and Cart shows the short items.
sonnet.q3: The charge key is the order id: Payment sends it as Idempotency-Key to the provider, and Payment has one charge row per order id (unique), so a repeat returns the existing charge. The provider cannot charge twice for the same key.
sonnet.q4: The order is set to Cancelled (out of stock), the full amount is refunded automatically, an OrderCancelled event is published and the customer is emailed. No partial order is fulfilled; refund status is recorded separately on the order.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only when Cart consumes OrderConfirmed. On any failure (short stock, declined, refused charge, cancellation) the cart is left unchanged.
sonnet.q6: Order moves it along: it calls Inventory and Payment over HTTP and consumes their events. The record of progress is the order's status in Order's own database (Placed, Awaiting payment, Confirmed, Rejected, Payment failed, Cancelled, plus refund status).
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment stores the event and charge status and writes a ChargeSucceeded or ChargeDeclined event to its outbox in the same transaction. A relay publishes it to the message broker, and Order consumes it.
sonnet.q8: Payment stores the provider event id with a unique key, so a repeated webhook returns 200 and changes nothing. Order also acts on a charge event only while the order is Awaiting payment, and a repeated claim returns 200 with no second stock decrement.
sonnet.q9: The hold is released immediately. Order, on the failed/declined payment, asks Inventory to release the hold. The reservation becomes Released, the reserved count drops and stock goes back on sale (a no-op if already released). The customer is told payment failed; the cart is unchanged and they may retry.
sonnet.q10: On ChargeSucceeded, Order asks Inventory to claim the hold. Inventory does one conditional update: it succeeds only if the reservation is still Held and expires_at is in the future. If yes, the order is confirmed; if no (hold lapsed), the order is cancelled and fully refunded.
sonnet.q11: Payment retries the refund with the same refund key (refund-order id) until the retry limit, which is not set. After that the refund stays Open in a needs-attention queue, ops are alerted, and RefundOpen is published, until a person resolves it. Order records the refund status on the order; the refund is tracked in Payment's refunds.
sonnet.q12: Order publishing OrderConfirmed (after Inventory claims the hold) causes it. The Cart service empties the cart on consuming that event.
